role: Software & Services Marketing Operations & AI Leader
headline: AI use cases that ship and get adopted, on top of one trusted view of marketing and commercial performance.
pitch: I turn AI into tools teams actually adopt, and I measure what they deliver. At flyExclusive, reporting to the Chief Commercial Officer, I built an LLM pipeline that has enriched about 500,000 CRM records; personalized outreach from it gets a 150% better response rate. My AI proposal and agreement tools save the sales team 1 to 2 hours per lead, and the conversational reporting I built is used by the entire executive leadership team and sales team. Underneath that, I led a HubSpot Enterprise data transformation (about 300 contact properties consolidated to 100, Master Data Management) and replaced Tableau and Airtable with tools I built myself. I drive adoption through biweekly office hours with the sales team, and I've done all this while serving as interim manager of a 20-person, ~$10M/month sales team. I'm based in Raleigh, one of the role's listed locations.

requirements.need: AI acumen: translate AI capabilities into practical business use cases and measurable outcomes
requirements.evidence: At flyExclusive I've shipped AI into daily work and tracked the results: an LLM enrichment pipeline that has enriched ~500,000 CRM records and powers lead scoring (150% better response rate on personalized outreach); AI proposal and agreement tools that save reps 1 to 2 hours per lead; and conversational reporting used by the entire executive leadership team and sales team. On this site I built a retrieval-augmented chat with an automated eval harness for grounding and refusals.

requirements.need: Define and drive the AI roadmap: productivity, customer insights, content, personalization, decision-making
requirements.evidence: I present the most pressing build needs to flyExclusive's Chief Commercial Officer every month, and the AI work already spans the categories in this role: content and personalization (LLM-written outreach), decision-making (lead scoring, the competitive-pricing app that set 2026 pricing), productivity (proposal tools), and insights (conversational reporting). Every build starts with a PRD and sign-off.

requirements.need: Unified data and analytics framework with trusted reporting and end-to-end performance visibility
requirements.evidence: I led flyExclusive's CRM data transformation (governance, ~300 contact properties consolidated to 100 sources of truth, deduplication, MDM) and run the ETL and daily data jobs on Azure. I built attribution frameworks and funnel dashboards that show marketing's contribution through to revenue. On this site, one channel definition is enforced in code and every report reads from it.

requirements.need: Integrated dashboards and analytics across the portfolio
requirements.evidence: Redesigned flyExclusive's retail performance dashboards for leadership; Tableau and Power BI; SQL, Python, and Databricks. At TRANZACT I ran multi-touch attribution and forecasting with commercial and finance leadership.

requirements.need: Scalable operating models, governance, data standards, and processes
requirements.evidence: I designed and enforced flyExclusive's CRM governance and onboarded 10 sales reps and 5 marketers onto it, and I run biweekly office hours for the sales team (a planned lesson, then open questions) to drive adoption. I cleaned a 500,000-contact list to the ~85,000 that could be marketed to compliantly, and I manage cookie consent and privacy policy updates.

requirements.need: Workflow automation and emerging technology for efficiency and scale
requirements.evidence: I replaced Tableau and Airtable with tools I built myself using agentic coding, cutting the cost to little more than cloud hosting, and I'm leading the replacement of HubSpot with an in-house tool. Automated enrichment and outreach drafting with LLMs and automated proposal generation. At TRANZACT I automated behavioral-data syncs into Iterable for 10+ lifecycle campaigns.

requirements.need: Lead large-scale cross-functional transformation with strong program management across multiple initiatives
requirements.evidence: At flyExclusive I've run a website migration, the HubSpot transformation, two tool replacements, and the AI sales tools across marketing, sales, and leadership, and now the HubSpot-to-in-house migration. I write a PRD and get sign-off before each build, run customer-facing work through iterative internal review, and manage tasks in Microsoft Planner with named reviewers and deadlines. I own a ~$500K-a-year marketing tools budget and manage the agency running ~$300K a month in digital ads. This has been at company scale, not global-enterprise scale.

requirements.need: Executive presence; influence stakeholders across a global, matrixed organization
requirements.evidence: Sales leadership wanted to email the largest list possible, but our domain reputation was rated "Bad" in Google Postmaster and mail was landing in spam. I made the case for trimming to engaged, opted-in contacts, won it, and open rates doubled. I present priorities to the Chief Commercial Officer monthly. I also lived and worked in India for two years with an international nonprofit, learning the local language and working closely with local colleagues; I haven't yet worked in a global corporate matrix.

requirements.need: Significant experience; software, SaaS, or services background preferred
requirements.evidence: Six years across marketing, CRM analytics, and AI, in private aviation and insurance rather than software. I bring the hands-on side the posting asks to measure: AI adoption, data quality, and automation I built myself.

featured.title: Resume Chat — grounded AI answers
featured.blurb: Retrieval-augmented chat over one source of truth, served server-side, with an automated eval harness for grounding and refusals. How I'd make AI trustworthy enough to adopt.

featured.title: UTM Journey Tracker — live
featured.blurb: Governance and data standards written as code, a data-quality report that counts every rule failure, and a real-time performance dashboard.

featured.title: From Attribution to Ad Spend
featured.blurb: End-to-end performance visibility turned into a decision: four attribution models compared, calibrated with lift tests, and turned into a budget plan.

items: Meet Marketing, Commercial Ops, RevOps, Digital, IT, and Customer Success leads; list every transformation program with its owner, milestone, and status.
Map the systems and data sources behind Software & Services reporting, and where definitions conflict between teams and regions.
Collect AI ideas already in flight or requested, and baseline the time teams spend on manual reporting and content work.
Publish one program dashboard (priorities, milestones, owners, risks) and a monthly review cadence with leadership.
Agree shared metric definitions and data standards, and start a data-quality scorecard.
Prioritize the AI roadmap by value and effort, and launch two pilots with clear success measures (for example, content drafting and insight summaries on pipeline data).
Ship the first integrated performance dashboard across the portfolio.
Report AI pilot results (hours saved, adoption, quality) and decide which to scale globally, with training and governance.
Roll out standardized processes and templates for the next wave of automation.
